newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait H1 budget surplus $2.4 billion - minister.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait H1 budget surplus $2.4 billion - minister.

text.p: Kuwait has earned 731 billion dinars ($2.4 billion) more than forecast in the first half of the current fiscal year to end-June, a minister was quoted on Wednesday as saying.

Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan, in a presentation of the 1997/98 budget, said the "deficit has entered a disappearing stage although it maintains its structural roots which need to be dealt with," al-Watan newspaper reported.

The report did not include a Gross Domestic Product (GDP) figure for 1996 which is estimated by economists at around 8.6 billion dinars by current prices compared with an official GDP of 7.95 billion dinars in 1995.

The current 4.21 billion dinar budget carries a projected net deficit of 1.21 billion dinars and a gross deficit of 1.51 billion. By law, 10 percent of total revenues is placed in an overseas nest egg investment fund.

The new draft budget, obtained by Reuters on Monday, put expenditure at 4.37 billion dinars with a net deficit of 1.17 billion dinars. Oil revenue was forecast at 2.56 billion dinars, almost unchanged from the previous year, while non-oil revenue was unchanged at 645 million dinars.
The added revenue in the current budget resulted from a rise in world oil prices last year and earlier this year above the conservative $13 a barrel Kuwait uses to calculate oil income.
OPEC-member Kuwait produces about two million barrels of oil a day. World prices soared more than $5 a barrel above Kuwait's projection before dropping by some 30 percent in recent months.

Kuwait, as part of efforts to balance the budget by 2000 and a privatisation plan, hopes to employ less foreigners and push Kuwaitis to seek non-government jobs. The state currently employs more than 90 percent of Kuwaitis in the workforce.
In real terms, state salaries in the welfare Gulf Arab country of some 720,000 Kuwaitis consume more than two-thirds of the oil revenue and account for almost half of the budget.
